title: Schumer Pushes Bill to Break Up Meatpacking Giants and Lower Grocery Prices
excerpt: The Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act would force Tyson, JBS, Cargill, and National Beef to choose a single protein line, targeting an industry where four companies control 85% of U.S. beef processing.
image_caption: A shopper selects packaged meat from a refrigerated grocery store display. U.S. ground beef prices have reached a record $6.83 per pound as Sen. Chuck Schumer pushes legislation to break up meatpacking conglomerates.
nri_angle: Chicken is a staple protein in many South Asian households, and any restructuring of the meatpacking industry could affect poultry prices. Greater competition could also benefit independent ethnic grocery retailers.
author: Diaspora Desk
